catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Structural, domain, and infrastructural architecture analysis of the cas_runner CLI, governance engines, telemetry adapters, and workspace bootstrapping.
analysis_limits: Targeted codebase snippet inspection without full execution environment
Analysis excludes agentic prompting and LLM loop logic to respect structural separation

system_map.overview: The cas_runner system is structured as a modular Python CLI and runtime engine that manages Continuous Architecture System (CAS) governance artifacts, verifies compliance, normalizes multi-tool telemetry, and orchestrates workspace state transitions.

layers.name: Presentation / CLI Layer
layers.purpose: Provides user entry points, workspace bootstrapping, and status dashboards.

layers.name: Application Service Layer
layers.purpose: Coordinates governance transitions, compliance checks, and flow execution.

layers.name: Domain & Engine Layer
layers.purpose: Defines domain entity models, health status calculations, transition rules, and compliance engines.

layers.name: Infrastructure & Adapter Layer
layers.purpose: Handles external telemetry format adaptation, client communication (LiteLLM/Mock), and filesystem serialization.

components.name: GovernanceActionEngine
components.role: Encapsulates state transitions and compliance validation mechanics via TransitionRegistry.

components.name: TelemetryAdapters
components.role: Normalizes agent execution spans across diverse vendors into a unified AgentTelemetrySpan model.

components.name: WorkspaceBootstrapper
components.role: Idempotently prepares workspace structures, symlinks, and settings blocks.

orchestration.execution_model: Synchronous CLI task execution driven by FlowRunner and GovernanceActionService invoking decoupled engine operations.

tools_and_integrations.name: Pydantic
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Strict domain schema validation and serialization

state_and_memory.name: CAS Knowledge Repository
state_and_memory.purpose: Stores governance rules, decisions, maps, models, and runtime profiles as markdown/json/yaml files.

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity Modeling
patterns.summary: Core governance entities and telemetry spans are declared as immutable or validated data models using Pydantic, enforcing structural contracts between CLI, engines, and disk storage.
patterns.intent: Ensure deterministic validation and serialization of architecture findings, actions, metrics, and health statuses across persistence boundaries.
patterns.context: The system processes governance artifacts, JSON metrics, and health states that originate from automated analysis runs and external agent logs.
forces: Dynamic inputs from varied external analysis tools can cause schema drift.
Business rules require strong typing for metrics, health states, and actions.
Manual validation logic across multiple service files creates duplication.
patterns.solution: Define domain models like TraceableMetric, GovernanceInventory, ComplianceFinding, and GovernanceAction within an isolated domain models module using Pydantic BaseModel.
implementation_signals: Classes inheriting from BaseModel or dataclass representations
Explicit field type annotations with nested metric structures
Strict parsing and serialization used across governance engine inputs

evidence.note: Complete canonical modeling of domain metrics, findings, and governance actions as typed entities.

benefits: Compile-time and runtime type safety across engine boundaries
Automatic serializability to JSON/YAML without manual dictionary conversion
Decoupled schema definitions that serve as living documentation
costs: Runtime validation overhead on high-throughput metric streams
Schema changes require careful version migrations if serialized to disk
failure_modes: Validation errors thrown at runtime when reading legacy artifact formats if backward compatibility defaults are missing

patterns.reuse_notes: Extract domain model classes into a dedicated module with zero runtime dependencies beyond standard schema libraries.

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine
patterns.summary: Separates state transition rules and governance lifecycles into an explicit registry class decoupled from action execution logic.
patterns.intent: Manage allowed status transitions for governance decisions and actions using a single source of truth.
patterns.context: Governance actions transition through multiple states (proposed, approved, rejected, deferred). Embedding validation inside workflow handlers leads to inconsistent rules.
forces: State transition rules must be easily auditable by architects.
Engine handlers should only execute transitions, not hardcode the matrix of allowed states.
Adding new states or conditional transitions should not require modifying the execution engine.
patterns.solution: Introduce a TransitionRegistry that indexes permissible transitions between states and provides explicit validation methods invoked by GovernanceActionEngine.
implementation_signals: A dedicated registry class maintaining transition dictionaries or transition graphs
Engine classes querying the registry before applying state updates
Clear exceptions raised on illegal state transitions

evidence.note: TransitionRegistry decouples state transitions from the GovernanceActionEngine's execution cycle.

benefits: Centralized validation of valid governance action lifecycles
Prevents illegal state transitions before side-effects are executed
Easy to write unit tests for valid and invalid state pairs in isolation
costs: Additional abstraction layer compared to straightforward conditional checks
failure_modes: Unhandled transitions can stall automated workflows if registry mappings become out of sync with new action types

patterns.reuse_notes: Adaptable to any lifecycle-driven domain model such as ADR approvals, issue tracking, and policy state machines.

patterns.name: Heterogeneous Telemetry Adapter Pipeline
patterns.summary: Standardizes varying external agent telemetry schemas into a unified internal span representation via specialized adapter classes.
patterns.intent: Normalize telemetry logs from disparate coding assistants and subagents into a common span model for cost calculation and workspace filtering.
patterns.context: Telemetry data originates from different CLI tools (Claude Code, Antigravity, custom coding agents) each having idiosyncratic timestamp formats, metadata keys, and token counters.
forces: Dashboard and health models require uniform metrics (cost, duration, provider).
Upstream telemetry log formats change independently across external tools.
Downstream analytics should not know about tool-specific serialization quirks.
patterns.solution: Implement targeted adapter classes (e.g. CodingAgentTelemetryAdapter, ClaudeCodeTelemetryAdapter, AntigravityTelemetryAdapter) translating raw payloads into AgentTelemetrySpan instances.
implementation_signals: Multiple adapter classes sharing a common target schema
Normalization helpers for epoch parsing, ISO strings, and provider inference
Decoupled cost estimation logic operating on the normalized model

evidence.note: Implements concrete adapter classes targeting AgentTelemetrySpan from diverse raw log streams.

benefits: Isolates external log schema volatility from core health and telemetry analytics
Extending support to a new agent runtime requires only adding a new adapter
Enables uniform cost and latency metrics calculation
costs: Requires maintaining individual adapter parsers as external log schemas evolve
failure_modes: Unmatched log formats may fail silent inference or result in fallback defaults with missing costs

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable whenever multi-vendor CLI runtimes or external monitoring endpoints must feed a consolidated observability pipeline.

patterns.name: Service-Engine Layer Separation
patterns.summary: Separates high-level workflow coordination and persistence from pure computational rule engines.
patterns.intent: Decouple IO, workspace coordination, and high-level execution flows from core compliance calculations and state transitions.
patterns.context: Governance tasks require inspecting files, executing policies, validating state, and persisting results. Blending these concerns makes automated testing slow and complex.
forces: Rule evaluation and compliance validation should be testable without filesystem IO.
CLI handlers require a single coarse-grained entrypoint to invoke actions.
Reusability of governance engines in multiple environments (CI, local CLI, webhook).
patterns.solution: Structure the domain using coarse-grained Service classes (GovernanceActionService) that coordinate I/O and orchestrate fine-grained Engines (ComplianceEngine, GovernanceActionEngine).
implementation_signals: Coexistence of *Service and *Engine classes in the governance namespace
Engines accept domain models and return results without directly handling CLI parameters
Services manage file retrieval, engine invocation, and logging

evidence.note: Coordinates application-level governance actions and delegates rule evaluations.
Performs state machine transitions and core action evaluations decoupled from service orchestration.
Evaluates architectural compliance rules against domain inputs.

benefits: High testability of engine logic using in-memory mock models
Clear boundaries between workflow management and rule execution
Services can be reused across CLI commands and background automations
costs: Slight boilerplate indirection passing data through service to engine
failure_modes: Leaking filesystem or network calls into the engine layer undermines purity

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard layered enterprise pattern for applications that enforce compliance, auditing, or validation rules.

patterns.name: Test Double Client Substitution
patterns.summary: Provides matching concrete client implementations for production communication and offline testing via a unified interface.
patterns.intent: Enable fast, deterministic test suites and offline CLI dry-runs without invoking external network endpoints.
patterns.context: The runner uses LiteLLM for network calls, but unit tests and CI validation workflows must run without API tokens or network latency.
forces: CI pipelines must validate runner flows without paid API credits.
Tests must verify error handling, schema parsing, and retry behaviors deterministically.
Business logic should not have branching conditionals checking for test environments.
patterns.solution: Maintain a production client (LiteLLMClient) and a mock client (MockLLMClient) implementing congruent communication signatures.
implementation_signals: Parallel client classes in the same package (e.g. litellm_client.py, mock_client.py)
Mock client returning canned responses or configurable fixtures matching real payloads

evidence.note: Mock implementation providing deterministic responses for offline runs and testing.

benefits: Zero external network dependencies during unit and integration test passes
Guarantees identical interface contract for consumers
costs: Mock client must be maintained whenever the real client API signature changes
failure_modes: Drift between mock responses and actual third-party API response shapes

patterns.reuse_notes: Use across all external API gateways (telemetry backends, LLM providers, git forges).

patterns.name: Idempotent Workspace Bootstrapping
patterns.summary: Initializes and updates project workspaces through declarative configuration merging and symlink or file copying mechanisms.
patterns.intent: Safely set up CAS governance structures in target repos without clobbering existing configuration files.
patterns.context: Users run CAS bootstrap in new or existing codebases where agent settings, markdown templates, and governance directories must coexist with project-specific settings.
forces: Re-running bootstrap must not overwrite customized project settings.
Symlink vs copy behavior depends on operating system and repo setup.
Users need visible verification checklists after workspace preparation.
patterns.solution: Encapsulate file creation, block merging (e.g., merge_cas_governance_block, merge_claude_settings), fallback link-copy strategies, and onboarding checklist generation in a dedicated bootstrap module.
implementation_signals: Functions with merge_* prefixes handling block preservation
Checklist rendering functions returning actionable onboarding status

evidence.note: Handles idempotent workspace configuration injection, link creation, and checklist formatting.

benefits: Safe repeated execution on existing repositories without data loss
Consistent directory conventions across all CAS-managed projects
Clear onboarding instructions rendered directly to the CLI
costs: String and JSON merge operations require defensive handling for invalid formats
failure_modes: Corrupted pre-existing configuration files could cause merge failures if parsing fails

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any scaffolding CLI tool that injects tooling configurations into existing user repositories.

anti_patterns.name: Unpinned CI Tooling Installation
symptoms: Workflows or setup scripts installing packages directly from latest main or without semantic version bounds
Transient CI failures caused by upstream breaking changes in build dependencies
impact: Non-reproducible pipeline execution and brittle automated governance checks
suggested_remediation: Pin all installer dependencies and GitHub actions to exact commit SHAs or explicit version constraints as enforced by specs/090-simplify-cicd-workflows/validate_workflows.py

anti_patterns.name: Leaky Telemetry Parsing Heuristics
symptoms: Spreading vendor-specific regex or timestamp parsing across dashboard presentation logic rather than isolating it within adapters
impact: High coupling between dashboard views and external agent log quirks, resulting in fragile reporting
suggested_remediation: Strictly route all raw telemetry ingestion through dedicated adapter classes that emit standardized AgentTelemetrySpan models

cross_cutting_concerns.scope: Across telemetry adapters, dashboard metrics, and CLI execution spans

cross_cutting_concerns.scope: Across bootstrap, action engine, and compliance checkers accessing cas-knowledge directories

open_questions.question: Will governance artifacts transition from raw filesystem YAML/JSON to an indexed database or embedded storage engine as repository size scales?
Is FlowRunner designed for concurrent multi-flow execution or strictly serial CLI invocations?
